blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (The switch to Paylane has no way back) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (The nightly settlement worker can fail without anyone seeing it) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The Stripe client is deleted and replaced by the Paylane client in the same
release. There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain. The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep a way back until Paylane has proven itself in production: keep the Stripe client behind a configuration switch (or a percentage rollout) for at least one weekly release cycle, and do not close the Stripe account until that window has passed without incident. Failure scenario: Paylane starts declining or timing out on authorizations two days after the release; the previous version can be redeployed, but it calls a Stripe account that was closed the day after the release, so no card payment can be taken by either provider and the only remedy is a new release against a provider that is failing. State the rollback path and the account closure criterion in the design.
findings.title: The switch to Paylane has no way back

findings.evidence:
A new worker, `settlement-worker`, runs at 02:00, fetches the day's Paylane
payments and matches them to orders. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Decide in the design how an operator learns that a run failed or did not run: a log line at start and end of each run with the counts fetched, matched and unmatched, a metric or heartbeat for the last successful run, and an alert when the CronJob fails or no successful run is recorded by a given hour. Failure scenario: the Paylane API is unreachable at 02:00 (or the CronJob is never scheduled after a manifest error); the job exits or never starts, nothing is written to the database and nothing alerts, so the day's payments stay unreconciled and the spec's alert to the finance channel for unmatched payments never fires either. Add a task for this monitoring to tasks.md.
findings.title: The nightly settlement worker can fail without anyone seeing it
